newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fire in HK housing block kills one, injures 25.
newsitem.headline: Fire in HK housing block kills one, injures 25.

text.p: Residents squatted on window ledges and clung to drainpipes to escape a fire that raged through a residential building in Hong Kong on Tuesday, killing an elderly woman and injuring at least 25 people.

The fire, which broke out on the sixth floor of a 20-storey block in Kowloon district around noon (0400 GMT), spread to a lower floor and firefighters were still battling to put out the blaze three hours later, a government spokeswoman said.
"One woman, 65 years old, has died and the latest news from the fire department is that 25 are injured...including children and firemen," the spokeswoman said.
"The situation is now under control, but firemen are still trying to put out the fire," she said.
Local radio said four people had been killed, but there was no immediate official confirmation.
The cause of the fire was not immediately known. It was also unclear how many children were hurt.
Thick billowing smoke forced residents on the upper floors to squat on window ledges and cling to external pipes crying out for help in scenes relayed live by local cable television.
Firemen were seen rescuing several women and ferrying a dog down an extension ladder.
Hong Kong has seen some of its worst building fires on record in recent months.
In November, a building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turned into an inferno, killing 39 people and injuring 81 in the territory's worst blaze in a building.
A fire in a karaoke bar in January killed 17 people in Kowloon's Tsimshatsui entertainment district.
